task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells are needed to test redistribution to the closest-profile teammate?
Which measurement, selection, and dependence risks affect spell-level usage-redistribution tests?
evidence_establishes: retrieve_history returned zero records (n_results = 0), so no earlier study by this project is available for this question in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer.
Whether any measurement, power, or regression-to-the-mean issue has been resolved or previously observed for this design.
Whether any prior analysis of absence spells in this data exists.
own_inferences: The stated units (148 spells, 11 cases) mean the effective sample for a between-case claim is about 11 absence cases; the 148 spells are clustered within those cases and within players, so they do not supply 148 independent tests.

'Closest profile' is undefined as posed. The question offers three alternative operationalisations (initiation profile, minutes, same-position minutes), and each yields a different predicted gainer, so the claim is not falsifiable until one is fixed in advance.

A teammate with more minutes or more initiations will tend to gain more raw volume after an absence mechanically, so a naive 'largest gainer' test would largely reproduce usage-share and minutes effects rather than a profile-similarity effect.

Gains measured on the play types the absent player used most are partly defined by the same pre-absence usage that selects the gainer, which makes the test circular unless the profile and the outcome are measured on separate windows.
Play-type labels in [source] database are derived from play-by-play; any reclassification or missing initiator attribution feeds directly into gain estimates.
uncertainties: Whether the 2025-26 regular season and playoffs (partial before 2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21 respectively) will be included, and how partial data are handled.
How many of the 11 cases have a clean pre-absence window and a clean post-absence window with enough initiations for the teammate ranking to be stable.
Whether roster or role changes between 2022-23 and 2025-26 shift play-type baselines enough to make pooled comparisons non-stationary.
The reliability of play-type initiation labels and of the initiator field itself has not been checked against the data_catalog or the source definitions in this setting.

historical_effect.explanation: No records were returned, so the retrieved history did not change the decision. The decision rests on the design constraints: 11 cases, an undefined profile-similarity measure, the mechanical minutes and volume confound, and the circularity between profile and outcome.

blocking_constraints.text: With 11 absence cases, a rank-based test of whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer has very little power to detect a moderate effect, and the 148 spells are clustered within cases.
Play-type initiations per teammate per spell may be too sparse to estimate gains reliably, especially for low-usage play types.
The closest-profile measure is not defined, and the three offered alternatives are not shown to be reliable across seasons or windows.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved (retrieve_history returned an empty list), so whether this question has been answered by this project cannot be determined from the available record.

risks.text: Eleven cases give very low power for any test of a ranked-gainer claim; spell-level counts overstate the effective sample.
Players selected as absence-period gainers or as 'closest profile' may have high pre-absence usage that regresses toward the mean, inflating apparent gains.

The teammate with the most minutes or initiations is expected to be the largest gainer by chance, so the chance-level baseline for 'largest gainer' must be computed before any hit rate is interpreted.
Minutes, role, position, lineup context, and injury-return timing all covary with both profile similarity and post-absence gain.
Play-type initiator labels and points are derived from play-by-play, and the gain outcome is built from the same derived labels used to define the profile.
If the profile is computed over a window that overlaps the absence period, the profile carries post-absence information into the test.
Mislabelled initiators or play types in the source play-by-play propagate into both the profile and the gain estimates.
Three profile definitions, several play types, and several gain metrics create many implicit comparisons; the analysis must fix one before seeing data.
Team roster and style changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 and between regular season and playoffs change baseline usage, so pooled gains may not be comparable.
No placebo comparison (for example a non-absent player on the same team with the same minutes) is defined, so a positive result could reflect generic redistribution rather than profile similarity.
A gain measured as a raw count rather than a rate has a mechanical floor and ceiling that favours high-minutes teammates.

design.estimand: Not defined as posed. The minimum viable estimand is the difference in play-type usage gain (post minus pre, rate per 100 team possessions, on a fixed window) between the teammate with the closest pre-absence profile and the teammate with the most minutes, averaged across absence cases, with the profile definition fixed in advance.
design.unit: Absence case (player-absence episode), with spells as nested observations within case.
design.sample: The 11 cases from the NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 data, restricted to regular-season spells with complete play-by-play; playoffs and the partial 2025-26 windows are excluded from the primary analysis.
design.power: Not computed. With 11 cases, a power analysis should be run before any test, and the study should be described as exploratory unless effect sizes and variance from pilot data justify a confirmatory design.
design.controls: Pre-absence minutes share, position match, lineup and on-court context, and baseline usage rate; a placebo teammate matched on minutes; profile windows that end before the absence begins.
design.falsification: The claim is falsified if the closest-profile teammate is not the largest gainer more often than the minutes-matched or random-teammate baseline, using a permutation null within case.
design.multiplicity: Fix one profile definition, one gain metric, and one primary play type before analysis; report the other two profile definitions and play types as secondary and adjust for them.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to a confirmatory study only if a pilot on a held-out subset of cases shows the profile-based ranking beats the minutes-matched and permutation baselines with a stable effect; otherwise report the question as untestable or inconclusive with these data.
design.data_version: NBA regular-season play-by-play and substitution intervals for 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 (the 2025-26 regular season used only after 2026-04-13); derived play-type graph records as built from the same play-by-play, with the build version recorded.
